name: Jozadak
overview: Jozadak was a male priest from the tribe of Levi, known primarily as the father of Jeshua who built the altar. His priestly role situates him within the Levitical line of service to God. This connection highlights his importance in the restoration of worship practices.
namesAndTitles: The name Jozadak means 'YHWH is righteous,' reflecting a theologically significant affirmation of God's justice. This proper name, recorded in Ezra 3:2, emphasizes the character and faithfulness attributed to him or his lineage.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Jozadak as the father of Jeshua, who played a key role in rebuilding the altar. He is also identified as a descendant of Aaron, the first high priest, establishing his Levitical priestly heritage.
scriptureSignificance: Jozadak's significance lies in his priestly lineage as a descendant of Aaron and as the father of Jeshua, who actively participated in restoring the altar during the post-exilic period. His role underscores the continuity of the Levitical priesthood and the reestablishment of proper worship after the Babylonian exile. Thus, he represents a vital link in the biblical narrative of restoration and faithfulness to God's covenant.
